comment: DryPrb - hardware probe, not a release effect. Tests whether one effect can leave a marker in a buffer that later effects in the chain can read without it reaching the output (the Div0 trick, docs/TEMPO-SYNC.md). Load it twice: Role SEND in an early slot writes a marker, Role READ in a later slot listens and plays a tone when it finds the marker. The input passes through unchanged.
gid_comment: 0x08 = Delay category -> Fx_DLY_, same as TempoPrb.
fxid_comment: Probe id (TempoPrb is 499), kept away from the pack's 480..496.

params.name: Role
params.comment: OFF = pass through. SEND = write the marker. READ = look for the marker and play a tone. Default OFF.

params.name: Where
params.comment: Which buffer half carries the marker. DRYR = Dry buffer right half (the idea), DRYL = Dry buffer left half, FXR = Fx buffer right half (control: that one the effects chain may mix into the output). Set SEND and READ the same. Default DRYR.

params.name: Shape
params.comment: Marker shape. DC = constant. ALT = alternates sign each sample (survives a DC filter). PULSE = on about 0.74 s, off about 0.74 s, like a bar marker. Default DC.

params.name: Amp
params.comment: Marker level on SEND (screen number / 100). Raise it to 100 to hunt for leaks into the output; READ finds anything above 0.25 percent of full scale.

params.name: Level
params.comment: Level of the tone READ plays. The input is never changed on SEND or OFF.
